raw_final_content:
The target is visually distinctive: a low spreading plant with many short, bright-red, densely hairy cylindrical “chenille” inflorescences and small ovate-serrate leaves. The close leaf image confirms that the target leaves are relatively small and toothed; the wide photograph shows a dwarf groundcover-like habit with many short red spikes.

This is a strong match to the dwarf cat-tail Acalypha commonly sold as Acalypha reptans, with horticultural nomenclature often overlapping A. chamaedrifolia (and related names). The much larger-leaved, long-pendulous A. hispida is a poorer visual fit. I am confident about the Acalypha/dwarf-cat-tail visual identity, while the exact accepted species name should carry a nomenclatural caveat.

The wide image contains several unrelated plants, so a model that describes all green foliage as one species would be making a grounding error.
